article_title: Visual Studio 2026 Graduates C++ Dynamic Debugging to General Availability, Letting Developers Inspect Optimized Code Without a Debug Build
summary: Submission approved with corrections: two quoted customer statements in the body paraphrase the source rather than reproduce it verbatim

findings.message: Quoted statement attributed to Michael Buschbeck does not match the source verbatim
findings.details: Article renders the quote as: "Dynamic Debugging lets me work in optimized builds while still being able to deoptimize and inspect code when needed." The source (source-0.html.gz, devblogs.microsoft.com/cppblog/c-dynamic-debugging-is-now-generally-available/) actually reads: "Dynamic Debugging is a game changer for C++ development. It lets me work in the optimized builds I actually need for large game codebases, while still being able to deoptimize and inspect code and runtime state when it matters. It removes a longstanding tradeoff between realistic runtime performance and a productive debugging experience." The article compresses and reworks the three-sentence quote into one sentence while presenting it inside quotation marks as a verbatim quote.

findings.message: Quoted statement attributed to Bryce Hutchings drops a word from the source
findings.details: Article renders the quote as: "It's seamless—you forget how much it's helping." The source (source-0.html.gz) actually reads: "It's so seamless you forget how much it's helping." The article drops the intensifier "so" and substitutes an em dash for the original sentence flow, so the quotation marks do not enclose the source's exact wording.

content_preview.title: Visual Studio 2026 Graduates C++ Dynamic Debugging to General Availability, Letting Developers Inspect Optimized Code Without a Debug Build
content_preview.summary: Microsoft's C++ Dynamic Debugging, which deoptimizes only the targeted stack frame, left preview on November 12, 2026 for all Visual Studio 2026 channels and MSVC Build Tools 14.52.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft announced that C++ Dynamic Debugging is now generally available in all Visual Studio 2026 channels and the Microsoft C++ (MSVC) Build Tools version 14.52, according to the [C++ Team Blog](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/cppblog/c-dynamic-debugging-is-now-generally-available/). The feature, which the team describes as addressing "a traditional development tradeoff" between debuggable and performant builds, lets developers inspect local variables, step through source line-by-...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear Briefing-length writeup (565 words, within the 300-800 range) covering a Microsoft C++ Team Blog announcement with appropriate context from the original 2025 preview post and independent trade-press coverage. Structure (Overview / What the feature does / From preview to general availability / What we don't know) is appropriate and the 'What we don't know' section honestly flags information the GA post omits rather than inventing it.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallback, no suspicious_patterns flags) and sha256-verified against manifest.json: source-0.html.gz (devblogs.microsoft.com/cppblog/c-dynamic-debugging-is-now-generally-available/, GA announcement dated November 12, 2026) confirms the GA claim, the 'all Visual Studio 2026 channels and MSVC Build Tools 14.52' language (verbatim in source), the feature mechanism description, the MSBuild/CMake/`/dynamicdeopt` enablement instructions, and Unreal Engine 5.6 / FastBuild / IncrediBuild compatibility (all verbatim in source). source-1.html.gz (devblogs.microsoft.com/cppblog/cpp-dynamic-debugging-full-debuggability-for-optimized-builds/, preview announcement dated March 19, 2025) confirms the Visual Studio 2022 v17.14 Preview 2 preview date, the verbatim quote 'dynamically deoptimizes code that you set breakpoints on or step into,' the per-frame deoptimization/[Deoptimized] tag behavior, and the build-time figures (1.05x-1.15x end-to-end, up to 1.8x iteration build for monolithic games) all verbatim in source. source-2.html.gz (infoq.com/news/2025/06/visual-studio-copilot-agent/, titled 'Visual Studio 2022 v17.14 Introduces Agent Mode and Advanced Copilot Assistance') confirms the article's InfoQ quote verbatim: 'to debug an optimised application build' that 'will be dynamically de-optimised in the background, allowing access to the variables and code structures as they are in the source code,' and 'it was required to perform a non-optimised build for debugging.' However, two customer quotes attributed to source-0 do not reproduce the source verbatim: the Michael Buschbeck quote is a condensed paraphrase of a three-sentence statement presented as a single verbatim sentence, and the Bryce Hutchings quote drops the word 'so' and alters punctuation. Both are documented as findings above and covered by a corrections record (neither appears in the headline, summary, or lead). Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article's subject is a Microsoft Visual Studio/MSVC C++ tooling feature; Anthropic/Claude is not the subject and is not named in the headline, summary, or lead (contributor_model is Claude Sonnet 5 but that is a provenance field, not a story subject).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Claim-accuracy pass: ran the quantifier/absence grep over title+summary+body_markdown. Every flagged quantifier claim ('only the targeted stack frame deoptimizes,' 'all Visual Studio 2026 channels,' 'all checks passed' style language) was cross-checked against the raw source text and confirmed accurate, including the build-time multipliers (1.05x-1.15x, up to 1.8x) which match source-1 verbatim. No fabricated specifics, no orphan sources (all 3 URLs appear in both article.sources and body_markdown), no date or timezone discrepancies. The only accuracy issue found is the two paraphrased-as-verbatim customer quotes noted above, which are subordinate body content, not headline/summary/lead claims.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no sensationalism, no AI self-reference, attributions are clearly sourced ('according to the C++ Team Blog,' 'the blog says,' 'an InfoQ report from June 2025').
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Searched src/content/articles/ for prior coverage of 'dynamic debugging' and recent Visual Studio articles in 2026-11; no existing article covers this GA announcement. Not a duplicate.
concerns: Two customer quotes in the body (Michael Buschbeck, Bryce Hutchings) are presented in quotation marks but paraphrase/condense the source's actual wording rather than reproducing it verbatim.
recommendations: Future submissions should copy direct quotes character-for-character from the source rather than condensing multi-sentence statements into a single quoted sentence.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Solid, accurately sourced Briefing on a real Microsoft C++ tooling GA announcement, with every substantive claim (dates, version numbers, build-time multipliers, feature mechanics) verified against the raw source snapshots. The sole defect is two body-level customer quotes that paraphrase rather than reproduce their source verbatim -- a single corrections note can honestly inform readers of the exact wording without affecting the headline, summary, or lead, so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS is the right verdict rather than REJECT. Featured candidacy: 0 - routine developer-tooling GA announcement of interest to a narrow C++/game-dev audience, not a broad or exceptional story.
